verdicts.quote: “Pumble uses OAuth2 in order to allow your app to access the API.”
verdicts.reason: Vendor auth docs explicitly specify OAuth2 and show exchanging an authorization code for “accessToken” and “botToken,” which fits a multi-tenant agent flow. ([cake-com.github.io](https://cake-com.github.io/pumble-node-sdk/authorization.html))

verdicts.quote: “If you wish to make your app Public, it needs to go through the review process… ‘Private’ app can be published immediately.”
verdicts.reason: Devs can self‑serve create/install apps, but publishing a Public app to the CAKE.com Marketplace requires platform review — exactly matching “app_review.” ([cake-com.github.io](https://cake-com.github.io/pumble-node-sdk/publish-to-marketplace.html))

The official API client covers core objects (messages, channels, users, workspace, calls, files) with key actions and scopes — broader than a handful, but not dozens of resources, so “moderate.” ([cake-com.github.io](https://cake-com.github.io/pumble-node-sdk/api-client.html))

verdicts.quote: “Pumble maintains a native MCP (Model Context Protocol) server hosted directly at pumble.com”
verdicts.reason: This is an official Pumble page documenting their own MCP server endpoint (mcp.pumble.com) and headers, so the MCP integration is vendor‑maintained (official). ([pumble.com](https://pumble.com/learn/pumble/ai-automation-guide/))

verdicts.quote: “If you login into Pumble you will see your App is installed and ready to use.”
verdicts.reason: It’s buildable today with self‑serve creds and docs; caveats include marketplace review for Public apps and stated rate limits, so “ready_with_caveats.” ([cake-com.github.io](https://cake-com.github.io/pumble-node-sdk/getting-started.html))
